citations.quote: A **finite-field hereditary Hall category** is a supplied small $\mathbb F_q$-linear abelian category $\mathcal A$ with the following properties: 1. For every pair $M,N$, $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M,N)$ is a finite-dimensional $\mathbb F_q$-vector space and the Yoneda extension group $\operatorname{YExt}^1(M,N)$ is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb F_q$. Its addition is Baer sum; scalar multiplication by $\lambda\in\mathbb F_q$ is pushout along $\lambda\operatorname{id}_N$. 2. For every $M,N$, $\operatorname{YExt}^2(M,N)=0$, where a two-fold extension is an exact sequence $0\to N\to E_1\to E_0\to M\to0$ modulo endpoint-fixed chain-map equivalence ([[def-n-fold-yoneda-extension]], [[def-equivalence-of-n-fold-extensions]]). 3. Smallness and the finiteness conditions of the Hall definition hold ([[def-hall-finitary-abelian-category]]). Here $\mathbb F_q$-linear means that every Hom set is a vector space and composition is bilinear. “Hereditary” in this page means exactly the stated vanishing of Yoneda $\operatorname{Ext}^2$; no projective or injective resolutions, derived-Ext identification, or choice principle is built into the definition. Under these conditions the Euler form used below is $$ \langle[M],[N]\rangle=\dim_{\mathbb F_q}\operatorname{Hom}(M,N) -\dim_{\mathbb F_q}\operatorname{YExt}^1(M,N). $$

Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small abelian category ([[def-abelian-category]]). Its set of isomorphism classes is denoted $\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal C)$. The **Grothendieck group** of $\mathcal C$ is $$ G_0(\mathcal C):=\mathbb Z[\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal C)]\big/\langle e_Y-e_X-e_Z:\ 0\to X\to Y\to Z\to 0\text{ is short exact in }\mathcal C\rangle. $$ where $\mathbb Z[\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal C)]$ is the free abelian group on that set ([[def-free-abelian-group]]) and $[X]$ denotes the image of the generator for the isomorphism class of $X$. Thus the defining relation is $[Y]=[X]+[Z]$ for every short exact sequence ([[def-exact-sequence-and-short-exact-sequence-in-an-abelian-category]]). This is the short-exact-sequence group, distinguished below from split Grothendieck groups of projectives. No free abelian group on the possibly class-sized collection of all objects is formed. The sequence $0\to0\to0\to0$ in particular gives $[0]=0$.

Let $\xi$ and $\eta$ be extensions of $M$ by $N$. Form their direct sum, pull it back along the diagonal $\Delta:M\to M\oplus M$, and then push that extension out along the codiagonal $\nabla:N\oplus N\to N$. The resulting extension of $M$ by $N$ is the **Baer sum** $[\xi]+[\eta]$. The direct sum alone has endpoints $N\oplus N$ and $M\oplus M$, so it is only an intermediate construction.

For fixed $M,N$ in an abelian category, assume that the equivalence classes of extensions of $M$ by $N$ form a set. With Baer sum, that set is an abelian group. Its zero is the split extension and the inverse of a class is its pushout along $-1_N$.

A linear combination of relations has a unique maximal path length; its terms of that length have distinct first-arrow/path/vector indices, so they cannot cancel unless their coefficients vanish. The composite of $P_1(V)\to P_0(V)\xrightarrow{s}E_0$ lands in $J=\ker(E_0\to V)=\operatorname{im}(E_1\to E_0)$. Projectivity of $P_1(V)$ lifts it through $E_1\twoheadrightarrow J$ to $t:P_1(V)\to E_1$. The split two-extension is zero in Yoneda $\operatorname{Ext}^2$, so the given extension is zero.

citations.quote: Let $\mathcal A$ be a small finitary abelian category in the sense of [[def-hall-finitary-abelian-category]], and let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit. Define the free $R$-module $$ H_{\mathcal A,R}:=\bigoplus_{[M]\in\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal A)}R[M], $$ where $[M]$ is a basis symbol for the isomorphism class of $M$. For objects $N,L$, let $$\operatorname{Mon}_{\mathcal A}(N,L):=\{f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(N,L): f\text{ is monic}\}.$$ This is a finite set by the Hom condition in [[def-hall-finitary-abelian-category]]. For $f,g$ in this set, write $f\sim_N g$ when $g=f\circ u$ for an isomorphism $u:N\to N$; this is an equivalence relation by [[def-isomorphism-groupoid-and-connected-category]]. The quotient set $\operatorname{Mon}_{\mathcal A}(N,L)/\sim_N$ represents exactly the subobjects of $L$ isomorphic to $N$: each class gives the usual subobject class from [[def-subobject-and-quotient-object]], and the mutual- factorisation theorem says two such monomorphisms give the same subobject exactly when they differ by such an isomorphism ([[thm-mutual-factorisation-defines-subobject-and-quotient-object-equivalence]]). Every subobject class with domain isomorphic to $N$ is represented by composing its monomorphism with an isomorphism from $N$, one class at a time. The cokernel quotient is independent of that representative by [[thm-the-quotient-is-independent-of-the-representing-monomorphism]] and [[def-the-quotient-of-an-object-by-a-subobject]]. Define $g^L_{M,N}$ to be the number of classes $[f]_{\sim_N}$ for which $\operatorname{coker}(f)\cong M$. The finiteness lemma below also proves that the resulting product has finite support. Extend the operation $$ [M]*[N]:=\sum_{[L]\in\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal A)}g^L_{M,N}[L] $$ $R$-bilinearly, mapping each natural number coefficient to its multiple of $1_R$. The order is fixed: the counted short exact sequence is $$ 0\longrightarrow N\longrightarrow L\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow0. $$ This is the **untwisted Hall product**. It does not use an Euler form, a square root of a field size, or division by automorphism cardinalities. The finite coefficient and finite-support claims needed for the operation to define a bilinear product are established in [[lem-untwisted-hall-product-finiteness]].

A **small finitary abelian category** for Hall multiplication is a small abelian category $\mathcal A$ (its object and morphism collections are sets, by [[def-small-locally-small-and-large-category]]), with abelian structure as in [[def-abelian-category]], in which the following sets are finite for every pair of objects $M,N$: 1. $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M,N)$; 2. $\operatorname{YExt}^{1}_{\mathcal A}(M,N)$, the set of Yoneda classes of short exact sequences $0\to N\to E\to M\to0$. Equivalence is the one-fold instance of the generated endpoint-fixed chain-map relation in [[def-equivalence-of-n-fold-extensions]]: chain maps are the identity on $N$ and $M$, and the relation is closed under reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity. A short exact sequence and its endpoint order use [[def-exact-sequence-and-short-exact-sequence-in-an-abelian-category]], [[def-extension-of-an-object-by-an-object-in-an-abelian-category]] and [[def-n-fold-yoneda-extension]]. One may instead supply a small skeleton $\mathcal A_0$ of an essentially small abelian category and perform the construction on $\mathcal A_0$. Here “essentially small” means that such a small equivalent category is part of the given data; the construction does not select representatives by an unstated choice principle. The isomorphism classes $\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal A_0)$ then form a set. No $\mathbb F_q$-linear structure, enough projectives or injectives, finite number of subobjects of every object, or identification with derived $\operatorname{Ext}^{1}$ is included in this definition. Subobjects are the monomorphism classes of [[def-subobject-and-quotient-object]], and quotients are the cokernels specified in [[def-the-quotient-of-an-object-by-a-subobject]].

A sequence of morphisms in an abelian category is **exact** when it is exact at every interior object in the sense of [[def-exactness-at-a-node]]. In particular, a composable triple $$0\to A\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{p}C\to 0$$ is a **short exact sequence** when it is exact at $A$, at $B$, and at $C$.
